title: Never be short tail risk: survival compounds
summary: The speaker managed over $2 billion of option premium at a large hedge fund. He says he could sleep because he never sold tail risk: every trade had a defined, known worst case. Returns come and go, but survival is what compounds. A large loss needs a much larger gain to recover.

steps.caption: The chart shows a loss on the account and the gain needed to get back to even.
The curve rises faster and faster: a 50% loss needs a 100% gain to recover. Tail losses are hard to undo.
Move the marker. A trade with an unlimited worst case can put you on the steep part of this curve.
Defining the risk on every trade keeps losses on the flat part of the curve, so the account survives to compound.

takeaways: Define the worst case of every trade before you enter it.
Do not sell tail risk: a single blow-up can end the account.
Returns come and go, but survival is what compounds.
caveats: The $2 billion premium figure and hedge fund role are the speaker's own claims and are not verified.
Part of the transcript is garbled; the lesson keeps only the clear points.
Define Your Risk is the speaker's brand; the video is partly promotional.
